tags.gist: Wants FDA to name four deployer capabilities, inventory, permissions checked at action time, institution-owned audit trail and a stop, as monitoring expectations manufacturers must enable.
Agrees that generative and especially agentic devices will carry more of their safety case after market than before.
Says greater postmarket reliance is reasonable only when monitoring can actually occur where the device is used, which depends on four institutional capabilities.
First, an inventory naming every generative function in use, its production version, an owner and authorized settings, or signals and recalls cannot be traced.
Second, written permissions for what the device may read, write, order or send, checked as each action occurs; for agentic functions, the whole safety case.
Third, a tamper-evident audit trail of inputs, outputs and actions held in the institution's custody, not only in manufacturer systems.
Fourth, the institution can immediately suspend or revoke the device's power to act, on its own authority, with who stopped it and why recorded.
Would frame these as outcomes the monitoring program must deliver rather than prescribed technology; devices that cannot support them forfeit reduced premarket evidence.
Makes log completeness and custody a precondition; adds deployer-side changes as reassessment triggers and denied or out-of-scope actions to sample review.
Accepts supervisory agents if independent of the device's manufacturer, institution-configured, able to deny out-of-scope actions, and themselves inventoried, logged and stoppable.
Divides accountability by visibility: manufacturers for performance and acting on signals, institutions for conditions of use, keeping inventory, permissions, log and stop, not validating models.
Wants any change-control approach to require manufacturers to notify deployers of model, prompt or tool changes before production, with a recordable version identifier.
Wants third-party model change notices routed through the manufacturer, which should be able to pin the version or roll it back for the deployer.
Would offset reduced human review with controls on action: declared default-deny action scopes, per-action checks, records of actions taken and denied, and an institutional stop.
Repeats that safety in use requires an institution able to list, limit, log and stop the device, and asks FDA to name those four expectations.
